savedState.boardInfo: Proof-of-concept causal model of The Sydney Plan (NSW Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure, Version 1, August 2026). The board synthesises the Plan’s seven priorities, twelve responses and implementation framework. It uses Australian English and is based only on the attached PDF. Compact wording and causal connections require careful human and subject-matter review before operational use.

pageInfo.overview: The board entry point summarises eight distinct causal domains and three implementation layers derived from The Sydney Plan.
pageInfo.p1: Drawn mainly from the Aboriginal Outcomes priority and Aboriginal-specific strategic outcomes across the Plan.
pageInfo.p2: Drawn mainly from the Housed priority and Responses 1–2 on housing supply, diversity, choice and affordability.
pageInfo.p3: Drawn mainly from the Prosperous priority and Responses 3, 4 and 6 on jobs, centres and industrial lands.
pageInfo.p4: Drawn mainly from the Connected priority and the Plan’s compact, transport-oriented spatial strategy.
pageInfo.p5: Drawn mainly from the Liveable priority and Responses 5 and 7 on vibrant centres and public open space.
pageInfo.p6: Drawn mainly from the Resilient priority and Responses 8–9 on natural assets, climate and hazards.
pageInfo.p7: Drawn mainly from Responses 10–12 on greenfield sequencing, non-urban land and infrastructure alignment.
pageInfo.p8: Drawn mainly from the Coordinated priority and Implementation section on governance, monitoring and adaptation.
pageInfo.p9: Level 1 implementation workstreams reproduce the Plan’s twelve response areas in compact form. Mapping is deferred to Step 2.
pageInfo.p10: Level 2 functions and partners synthesise the governance and partnership roles described in the Implementation section. Mapping is deferred to Step 2.
pageInfo.p11: No-level cross-cutting planning competencies required across multiple responses. Mapping is deferred to Step 2.
pageInfo.p12: Combined purpose, scope, assumptions, source and limitations page.
pageInfo.p13: Illustrative monitoring and evaluation page based on the Plan’s implementation framework and Table 5 metrics.
pageInfo.final: Six final outcomes synthesise the Plan’s seven priorities without implying formal endorsement or certification.

docContent.p12:
Purpose

This proof-of-concept DoView translates the August 2026 Sydney Plan into a causal planning model that connects its seven priorities, twelve responses, implementation arrangements and monitoring approach.

Scope

The board covers the Sydney region and the Plan’s twenty-year land-use direction for housing, jobs, centres, transport access, open space, natural assets, hazards, greenfield sequencing, non-urban land, infrastructure and governance. Step 1 contains This–Then links and implementation pages but deliberately defers How-link mapping.

Assumptions

  • The Plan’s strategic outcomes and responses are treated as the authoritative source for this draft.
  • Compact box wording necessarily synthesises longer policy statements.
  • Causal links express plausible planning dependencies rather than independently verified effects.
  • Population, jobs, housing and infrastructure projections may change as the Plan is monitored and updated.

Sources

Primary source: NSW Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure, The Sydney Plan, Version 1, August 2026, supplied by the user as the-sydney-plan.pdf. Key source sections include Priorities (pp. 21–60), Responses (pp. 61–96) and Implementation (pp. 97–98).

Cautions and limitations

This is an AI-assisted proof of concept, not an official NSW Government board and not an independent evaluation. It does not reproduce the Plan’s maps, technical appendices, local spatial guidance or full action schedule. Strategic, causal, feasibility and organisational judgements require review by the Department, councils, Aboriginal communities, infrastructure providers and other affected parties before operational use.
docContent.p13:
Illustrative monitoring framework

The Plan proposes an indicators tracker, actions tracker, annual progress update, report card and spatial viewer. The following live references bring selected board measures and evaluation questions into one review page.

Plan-level outcomes

Selected measures

Evaluation questions

Example causal relationship

Review rhythm

Review action delivery and metrics annually; test equity, feasibility, environmental and infrastructure effects at each major plan update; and use findings to adjust local planning strategies, sequencing and investment. Disaggregate indicators where possible so regional improvement does not conceal unequal outcomes.
docContent.p14:
Using DoView Boards and Disclaimer

See the disclaimer section below.

The DoView Board prompt and the DoView Board built within this DoView Board prototype app are provided free of charge so that anyone can experiment with DoView Boards and explore for themselves how they can answer the 20 key questions that anyone running or overseeing an organization needs to answer. See https://doviewplanning.org/doviewboards.

Walk-Through

To get a walk-through for using DoView Boards, see https://doviewplanning.org/walkthrough.

Accessing Consulting or Training

We can provide consulting or training on integrating the use of DoView Boards into your existing planning, implementation and reporting workflows in business, government, or nonprofit settings. See https://doviewplanning.org/offerings.

Adapting the DoView Board Prototype App to your setting

This DoView Board is being used within the DoView Board prototype app. It is a free of charge app that runs inside any browser window and can be used for piloting, testing, proof-of-concept and for use where confidential information is not being included and where there is a low security risk.

The DoView Board app is an open-source developer project under an Apache-2.0 open-source license. See https://github.com/doviewplanning/official-doview-boards. The wider DoView Planning methodology and DoView® trademarks are governed separately. See https://doviewplanning.org/trademarkuse.

Because it is an open-source project, any developer can extend, harden, adapt, or include features of the DoView Board app in other planning products or systems to suit specific deployment requirements. For example, adding enhanced stability, scalability, security, authentication, data handling, or integration features needed for production use, sensitive content, or higher-security environments. If you are looking to deploy DoView Boards in a live operational setting, you can work with any developer to tailor the app to your needs. You can also get in touch with us for advice and methodological input into the best way for you to adapt and extend your use of DoView Boards in your particular setting. https://doviewplanning.org/contact.

Disclaimer

DoView Boards are provided for planning and illustrative purposes only. The content of any DoView Board does not constitute professional advice of any kind, including but not limited to legal, financial, medical, strategic, or organizational advice. No warranty is given as to the accuracy, completeness, or fitness for purpose of any content. The usual precautions for AI-generated material need to be taken. Dr Paul Duignan, DoViewPlanning.org, The Ideas Web Ltd, DoView Corporation Ltd and any associated parties accept no liability whatsoever for any loss, damage, or adverse outcome arising directly or indirectly from the use of, or reliance on, any DoView Board or its contents. Use entirely at your own risk.

Please note that this DoView Board is in an interactive HTML file and contains active JavaScript so the board can work. Only open boards from sources you trust. Read-only copies disable editing through the board interface but are not security protection.

measures.title: Five-year housing supply targets
measures.mainText: Track completions against the current five-year housing targets.

measures.title: Relative increase in attached housing
measures.mainText: Track change in attached and medium-density housing across Sydney.

measures.title: Feasible housing supply by LGA
measures.mainText: Track whether each local government area maintains sufficient feasible housing capacity.

measures.title: Affordable and Aboriginal housing delivered
measures.mainText: Track affordable housing units and new dedicated housing for Aboriginal peoples.

measures.title: Jobs growth by centre and LGA
measures.mainText: Track progress against ten- and twenty-year employment targets.

measures.title: Development-ready industrial land pipeline
measures.mainText: Track progress toward 250 hectares of development-ready industrial land each year.

measures.title: Dwellings near quality public open space
measures.mainText: Track dwellings within 400 metres of local public open space of at least 3,000 square metres.

measures.title: Tree canopy coverage across Sydney
measures.mainText: Track progress toward 40% tree canopy across Sydney.

evalQuestions.questionText: How effectively are Aboriginal priorities and knowledge shaping planning decisions?
evalQuestions.mainText: Examine influence, not only participation, across regional and local planning.

evalQuestions.questionText: Is housing growth becoming more feasible, diverse and affordable?
evalQuestions.mainText: Assess delivery, feasibility, diversity, tenure and access together.

evalQuestions.questionText: Are jobs and services becoming more accessible across Sydney?
evalQuestions.mainText: Test whether western Sydney and disadvantaged communities gain better access to opportunity.

evalQuestions.questionText: Does growth improve place vibrancy and equitable open-space access?
evalQuestions.mainText: Review cultural life, public-realm quality, safety and access alongside density.

evalQuestions.questionText: Are environmental and hazard risks reducing as growth proceeds?
evalQuestions.mainText: Assess avoidance, restoration, adaptation and residual risk over time.

evalQuestions.questionText: How well are monitoring findings changing plans and investment?
evalQuestions.mainText: Test whether reporting results in timely adjustment rather than passive compliance.
